thread:
Marie: Quick sync — starting a short thread about unifying tenant fanout + authz in the console. Goal: avoid duplicate per-tenant query passes and make SLA-priority routes predictable. Thoughts?
Alex: +1. Do we collapse authz into the main query executor or keep it as a separate prefilter?
Sam: Leaning toward single-pass: authz predicate in the projection layer so we can short-circuit denied tenants and avoid extra reads. Fewer hops.
Kai: I worry about cacheability. Separate prefilter = central cache (token->perms) we can reuse across many queries for high-QPS tenants.
Marie: Tradeoffs noted. Hybrid idea: a cached prefilter fast-path for cache hits, fallback to executor-level predicate on cache miss. SLO target for prefilter path: p95 < 3ms.
Alex: Implementation sketch:
```
prefilter -> cache lookup -> if hit route to fast-path executor
else route to main executor (auth predicate evaluated inline)
```
We also need telemetry per-path.
Sam: Cache invalidation is the big concern — role/permission changes cause churn. How tolerant are we of short-lived stale allow decisions?
Kai: We can use epoched permission tokens. Bump epoch on role change and reject/refresh results tied to old epoch. Limits stale window.
Marie: Good. Action items: 1) add telemetry: path, cache_hit, auth_epoch; 2) prototype prefilter fast-path under 3ms budget; 3) SRE to run load tests with role-change churn. Volunteers?
Alex: I'll own telemetry + the per-route dashboards.
Sam: I'll prototype executor predicate fallback and measure delta in latency.
Kai: I'll add epoch bumping to the perf harness and simulate role churn.
InfraBot: Deploy bot: created branch 'authz-prefilter-proto' and scheduled nightly perf run.
Marie: Great, thanks — let's sync Thurs 09:00 to review perf runs and decide next steps. :thumbsup:
